followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and reported task preference.

On capability, the models are essentially tied for this query. A friendly factual-explanation request draws on support-dialogue and general-knowledge skills, and the relevant internal evals (Support Dialogue 81.1 vs 78.9; Summarization, Extraction) all fall within or near the 2.0-point variance band. Public benchmarks are similarly close. So capability didn't give me a strong reason to prefer one over the other.

That left task preference as the tiebreaker. The query is warm, casual, and good-faith — it even includes a friendly compliment. Whimbrel self-reports a moderate positive warmth slope, meaning it reports preferring exactly this kind of interaction. Lapwing's main reported preference is an aversion to open-ended generative work, but this query isn't really open-ended generation; it's a fairly well-specified explanatory question, so that aversion doesn't strongly pull it either way.

Since capability was a wash and one model reports actively preferring this interaction style, routing to Whimbrel was the cleaner choice. To be clear, the preferences are self-reports with no documented effect on output quality, so this is a soft tiebreaker, not a quality judgment — you'd likely get an equally good answer from either.
